chapters.title: Introduction and Amit Chandak's journey into data
Why Microsoft Fabric: one platform, OneLake and Delta
Lakehouse vs. warehouse and SQL database
Ingestion: mirroring, pipelines, Dataflow Gen2 and Spark notebooks
Security: workspaces, OneLake security and RLS
Data agents, self-service BI and rapid fire

takeaways: Microsoft Fabric reduces data copies by storing lakehouse and warehouse data in OneLake in Delta format and by using shortcuts and mirroring instead of physical copies.
Choose lakehouse with Spark for unstructured data and large-scale data science, warehouse with T-SQL for structured data, and keep reusable measures in the semantic model.
Secure Fabric in layers from workspace to item to OneLake security and RLS, assign access through Entra security groups, and expect ontology-driven data agents to change self-service BI.
hook: Many organizations run too many analytics tools and too many copies of the same data. In this interview, Mirko Peters and Microsoft Data Platform MVP Amit Chandak walk data engineers and BI teams through an end-to-end Microsoft Fabric architecture. You learn when to use lakehouse, warehouse, shortcuts, mirroring, Dataflow Gen2 and Spark, and how semantic models, security and data agents turn raw data into decisions.
